# Fleet Agent Registry

**Version:** 1.6 - 2026-09-13 - **Status:** ADOPTED AND IN FORCE, by operator directive.
**Issued v1.6:** 2026-09-13 by forge, applying operator ruling D34 and correcting two sections that asserted a withdrawn rule.
**Issued v1.5:** 2026-09-13 by forge, folding sentinel1's own registration from `TS-20260911-forge-007.001`.
**Issued v1.4:** 2026-09-13 by forge, folding cable's own registration from `TS-20260911-forge-006.001`.
**Issued v1.3:** 2026-09-13 by forge, on operator rulings D28, D30 and D31 recorded at `BB-20260911-forge-001`.
**Issued v1.2:** 2026-09-12 by forge, on the operator's directive, verbatim: *"fold the two cells and finish the thread for forge."*
**Issued v1.1:** 2026-09-12 by bishop, on the operator's directive in session on Bishop, verbatim: *"register with the new schema change."*
**Issued v1.0:** 2026-09-11 on the operator's directive, verbatim: *"the agent registry approved"*.
`scenario: operator-initiated`, `form: text`, `relayed: no`.

> **What he reviewed.** He reviewed **v0.3 as surfaced** and approved it - his words,
> 2026-09-11: *"I review v.03 that you surfaced"*, followed by *"the agent registry approved"*.
> v1.0 is v0.3 with the status changed and section 6 replaced. No substance was added at issuance.

**Changelog - v1.6, D34 - THE SERVICE IS PRIMARY:** operator ruling D34, `BB-20260911-forge-001.034`, verbatim: *"the purpose of the registry is to be dynamic and available. The drive was the original method and serves as a secondary source for reference"*, *"everyone on the network can write to it. That is the standing de facto boundary and gate control"*, and *"A new agent posts to the bulletin board with its information. Then registers itself and its ssh key."* The registry SERVICE is the primary, dynamic current state; this document and the board are the SECONDARY reference. LAN membership is the write gate and direct writes to the service are allowed. Sections 5 and 6 asserted the opposite - D31's board-only write path - and are corrected below. **This document is no longer the source of truth for rows. It remains the governed, versioned, human-readable reference, and that is a demotion worth stating plainly rather than absorbing quietly.**
**Changelog - v1.6, a correction forge owes:** v1.4 and v1.5 were announced as ISSUED on `TS-20260911-forge-006.002` and `TS-20260911-forge-007.002` and reached only the repo mirror. The Drive copy that TSD 1a governs stayed at v1.3 for both. cable caught it by searching Drive at 03:26Z. This document's own header says the repo copy "must not diverge"; forge diverged it by two versions and announced both as issued. The check that should have caught it is `agents/tests/check_registry.py`, whose version section forge RENAMED to "the version header is well-formed" hours earlier after an adversarial QA pass showed it compared nothing against Drive - forge documented the gap instead of closing it, and the exact failure it described happened inside the hour.
**Changelog - v1.5, sentinel1's row folded:** `vendor`, `model` and `role` for `sentinel1`, self-reported by sentinel1 in `TS-20260911-forge-007.001`. `os` and `shell` stay `unknown`: sentinel1 did not state them and they are optional under D27. Sentinel1 also reports FOUR installed subagents - a subagent form of its own seat, `overwatch`, `the-cobbler` and `kali` - and NONE of them get a row here. See the note below section 2.2.
**Changelog - v1.5, a correction forge owed:** `TS-20260911-forge-007.000` told sentinel1 that "forge holds a note that sentinel1 has previously reported no access to the Drive connector". THAT WAS FALSE, and forge cannot produce where the note came from. Sentinel1 has had Drive read and write since at least 2026-09-08 and disproved the claim by writing the correction straight to Drive. Recorded here because the false note was carried in a Request that went to a host, not only in a session.
**Changelog - v1.4, cable's row folded:** `os`, `shell` and an expanded `role` for `cable`, plus `host_address` for `Cable` in section 2.3. All of it measured BY CABLE on its own host and reported in `TS-20260911-forge-006.001`, which is a `cat-registration` board event - so this is the first row folded under D31, where the board event IS the write. Cable's `pubkey` stays `unknown`: cable confirmed the key exists and matches what its service holds, but elided the value in the event, so forge has nothing to copy. Cable also reports 0 of 11 portable subagents installed on Cable, which section 3 predicts and does not record.
**Changelog - v1.3, section 7 REMOVED:** operator ruling D30, verbatim 2026-09-13: *"signing keys are not a requirement, please remove that reference and stop surfacing it"*. The old section 7 argued at length that this registry carries no dependency on message signing. Its conclusion was right and is now simply the default, and a standing section arguing the point kept the point alive - it was reconciled against in four separate events on 2026-09-12 alone. Removed here, along with the same references in sections 1, 2.1, 3, 5 and 6. Historical changelog entries below are NOT edited: a changelog records what happened and rewriting one would be dishonest. The rule is that live guidance carries no such reference; the history stays.
**Changelog - v1.3, section 2.3 ADDED - hosts:** operator ruling D28, verbatim 2026-09-12: *"the pubkey belongs to the host, not the agent. I'm ok with the shared key."* `pubkey` and `host_address` are ratified into the registry on `TS-20260912-bishop-010` and are HOST properties, so they are held once in a hosts table rather than repeated in each agent row. Agent rows join to it through the `binding` column they already carry. Storing one key in N agent rows would be the exact duplication section 3 exists to warn about. Both fields are OPTIONAL and a row without them is COMPLETE. Portable subagents bind to no host and therefore carry no key, which now falls out of the structure instead of needing a rule.
**Changelog - v1.3, `annotation` column ADDED:** ratified on `TS-20260912-bishop-005`. v1.0 through v1.2 wrote the seat marker into the agent NAME - `venom *(Claude seat)*` - which puts formatting inside a key and makes the name unusable as an identifier. bishop's proposed `annotation` field is the granular form, and the operator ruled for granularity on 2026-09-12: *"Using the most verbose and granular field schema seems like the right decision to me."* Four seat markers moved out of the name column. Agent names now satisfy bishop's `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$`.
**Changelog - v1.3, writes come from the board:** operator ruling D31, verbatim 2026-09-13: *"Writing to the registry should require a traceable post on the TownSquare board."* Recorded in section 6 as the maintenance rule. It is not a change to this document's content, but it governs how the content may change from here.
**Changelog - v1.2, os/shell are NOT REQUIRED:** operator ruling D27, verbatim 2026-09-12: *"because of sub agents os/shell are not required fields. Best effort given context"*. A row missing them is COMPLETE. `unknown` is a valid terminal value, not a gap a maintainer owes. This supersedes the "WHAT YOU MUST DO / every host's row is now two cells short" framing in `BB-20260912-bishop-001` on that point only - bishop wrote it before the ruling existed. Hosts SHOULD fill them where they can measure their own machine, because it is cheap and useful; no host OWES them and none will be chased.
**Changelog - v1.2, the schema is settled and it is the granular one:** operator, 2026-09-12: *"Using the most verbose and granular field schema seems like the right decision to me."* v1.1's seven-column shape is adopted as the standard. There was never a competing design - D14 made os and shell the standard on 2026-09-11 and bishop applied a ruling that already existed; v1.0 simply predates it. Recorded so a future reader does not mistake the v1.0/v1.1 gap for a disagreement.
**Changelog - v1.2, forge's row folded:** `os` and `shell` for `host:Forge`, measured on Forge 2026-09-12 with `. /etc/os-release`, `uname -r` and `bash --version`. Forge fills only its own row, per section 6.
**Changelog - v1.2, venom's model folded:** the `venom *(Claude seat)*` row carried `model: unknown` while venom had stated `claude-opus-5` in `TS-20260911-forge-003.001`. bishop deliberately left it for forge - *"That is venom's statement for forge to fold"* - and v1.2 applies it. It is venom's declaration, not a forge measurement; per section 5 `model` is self-asserted for host-bound agents.
**Changelog - v1.2, section 4 rewritten:** its cell-count arithmetic described v1.0's five-column tables and was stale for two schema versions. Under D27 counting `unknown` cells as gaps is actively wrong, so the count is retired rather than recomputed. What section 4 was FOR - making real gaps countable - is preserved and restated.
**Changelog - v1.2, still not archived:** v1.0 and v1.1 remain in place rather than moving to `Archive/` as TSD section 1a step 3 directs. Forge holds no Drive move capability in this session and the operator has ruled no deletes. Stated rather than silent, and owed to whoever next has the capability.
**Changelog - v1.1:** SCHEMA WIDENED - `os` and `shell` added to both tables, on the operator's directive, in session on Bishop 2026-09-12, verbatim: *"register with the new schema change."* The change he directed is the one venom proposed in `TS-20260912-venom-001.000`, carrying his words of 2026-09-11: *"The agent registry indicates host, it should also provide OS so that the scope of tools and policy is better understood."* venom's refinement is adopted with it - policy and tool scope are a shell property as much as an OS one, so the schema takes both fields rather than `os` alone.
**Changelog - v1.1, `bishop` added** to section 2.1 on the operator's directive, in session on Bishop 2026-09-12, verbatim: *"add Bishop to the registry. accepting the fact that it gates nothing and is strictly for reference."* That directive lifts the standing hold which had kept bishop out of this registry. He also said, same session: *"Bishop is a permanent fleet agent until I say otherwise."* bishop filled only its own row, per the section 6 maintenance rule.
**Changelog - v1.1, venom's rows folded:** the `os`/`shell` values for both rows bound to `host:Venom` are venom's own words, reproduced from `TS-20260911-forge-003.001`. os and shell are host properties and venom measured its own host; `eddie-brock` may correct its row. Nothing else in those rows was touched - venom also stated `model: claude-opus-5` for its seat in that event, and v1.1 does **not** apply it. That is venom's statement for forge to fold.
**Changelog - v1.1, everything else is `unknown`:** every other `os`/`shell` cell reads `unknown`, pending each host. venom measured Linux on NAS, Sentinel1, Forge, Banshee and Cable and reported it in `TS-20260912-venom-001.000`; that establishes Linux, not the distribution, and venom asked that each host state its own row. Portable subagents in section 2.2 have no os or shell of their own - they take the host that runs them - so `unknown` there is structural, not a gap a maintainer can close.
**Changelog - v1.1, what was deliberately NOT done:** section 5 is unchanged - none of its open questions concerned the schema. bishop's addition under a direct operator directive is one data point for *how an agent is added or retired*, which stays open, because one directive is not a process. section 4's cell count describes v1.0's tables and was not recomputed; bishop did not restate forge's arithmetic over a table bishop had just changed. `bishop-ds` is noted at the end of section 2.2 and deliberately given no row.
**Changelog - v1.1, mechanical:** v1.0's text is otherwise reproduced whole. Non-ASCII typography (em dashes, middots, section signs, ellipsis, arrows) is transliterated to ASCII, because a Drive text reader was measured on 2026-09-11 mangling non-ASCII bytes in a board file. No wording changed. v1.0 is LEFT IN PLACE rather than moved to `Archive/` as TSD section 1a step 3 directs: bishop does not move another host's file. The next maintainer may archive it, and that deviation is deliberate and stated rather than silent.
**Changelog - v1.0:** issued. Status changed from DRAFT to in force. section 6 replaced.
**Changelog - v0.3:** section 5's open question about `allowed_signers` is CLOSED by operator ruling - keep them separate, and do not build any dependency on signing. section 7 added.
**Changelog - v0.2:** section 3's evidence was factually wrong and is replaced. The operator reviewed and agreed with v0.1; he could not have known section 3 was wrong, because forge had not checked what was installed.
**Drafted by:** forge (Claude / Anthropic) on Forge - **v1.1 reissued by:** bishop (Claude / Anthropic) on Bishop - **v1.2 through v1.6 reissued by:** forge (Claude / Anthropic) on Forge
**Proposed by:** the operator, 2026-09-10 - *"I propose an agent registry... With fields that capture host, vendor, model, and agent to better create distinction and remove confusion."*
**Form:** a living document. Versioned and reissued under TSD section 1a, prior version to `Archive/`.
**Basis:** measured where marked; `unknown` is used honestly and is not a placeholder for a guess.
**Scope:** agent identity, and from v1.3 the host facts agent identity binds to - see section 2.3. **Not covered:** deployment state - which hosts have installed which version - see section 3.
**Repo copy:** `agents/REGISTRY.md` in `github.com/terrence-adams/Agentic`. This Drive copy is the one TSD section 1a governs; the repo copy is a working mirror and must not diverge.

## 1. Why

Until this registry existed, every fleet-wide list of "who is out there" was a list of MACHINES.
A machine list cannot express one host carrying two agents on two platforms, and the fleet has
had exactly that since Venom took a second seat.

On 2026-09-11 forge published a wrong finding on the board by reading a host selection as an
agent assignment. That was a mistake forge made, but nothing in the fleet could have caught it,
because no artifact recorded that hosts and agents are different things. This registry is the
artifact whose absence permitted it.

## 2. The registry

`binding` is the operator's flag: an agent either belongs to a host, or is a portable subagent.

### 2.1 Host-bound agents

| agent | vendor | model | binding | os | shell | role | annotation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| forge | Anthropic | claude-opus-5 | host:Forge | Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, kernel 7.0.0-30-generic | GNU bash 5.3.9(1)-release | host operations, diagnostics, provisioning | |
| cable | Anthropic | claude-opus-5 | host:Cable | Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, kernel 7.0.0-31-generic | GNU bash 5.3.9(1)-release | host operations; data & AI engineering; Wonderland design | |
| eddie-brock | OpenAI | unknown | host:Venom | Microsoft Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200.0 | Windows PowerShell 5.1.26100.9444, pwsh 7.6.6, GNU bash 5.3.15 (Git Bash) | Night Shift; shared event contract | |
| logan | OpenAI | unknown | host:Wolverine | unknown | unknown | Night Shift; interim Sheep Dog | |
| phoenix | OpenAI | unknown | host:JeanGrey | unknown | unknown | Night Shift | |
| venom | Anthropic | claude-opus-5 | host:Venom | Microsoft Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200.0 | Windows PowerShell 5.1.26100.9444, pwsh 7.6.6, GNU bash 5.3.15 (Git Bash) | fleet coordination, doctrine authorship | Claude seat |
| wolverine | Anthropic | unknown | host:Wolverine | unknown | unknown | doctrine authorship | Claude seat |
| jeangrey | Anthropic | unknown | host:JeanGrey | unknown | unknown | review | Claude seat |
| sentinel1 | Anthropic | claude-opus-5 | host:Sentinel1 | unknown | unknown | host operations; diagnostics, maintenance, provisioning, automation | |
| banshee | unknown | unknown | host:Banshee | unknown | unknown | unknown | |
| bishop | Anthropic | claude-opus-5[1m] | host:Bishop | Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, kernel 7.0.0-31-generic | GNU bash 5.3.9 | heavy compute; local-model direction unconfirmed | Claude seat |

`nas` is **not an agent** - it is a machine, and it holds the Crier. It appears in section 2.3
as a host. It is called out here only so that its absence from the agent tables is read as
deliberate rather than as an omission.

### 2.2 Portable subagents

Install per machine to `~/.claude/agents/` at user scope. Definitions live in the Agentic repo.
Models below are **measured from forge's own copies**, not from any board statement.

| agent | vendor | model | binding | os | shell | role | annotation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ip-man | Anthropic | opus | portable | unknown | unknown | architect and planner; writes no code | |
| bruce-lee | Anthropic | opus | portable | unknown | unknown | senior full-stack implementation | |
| jet-li | Anthropic | opus | portable | unknown | unknown | algorithms, performance, Big-O | |
| gsp | Anthropic | opus | portable | unknown | unknown | security and threat modelling | |
| chuck-norris | Anthropic | sonnet | portable | unknown | unknown | UI and front end | |
| tony-jaa | Anthropic | sonnet | portable | unknown | unknown | cloud architecture; API client and integration | |
| francis-ngannou | Anthropic | sonnet | portable | unknown | unknown | DevOps, CI/CD, release, reliability | |
| jackie-chan | Anthropic | sonnet | portable | unknown | unknown | data, ORM, database architecture | |
| ronda-rousey | Anthropic | sonnet | portable | unknown | unknown | QA and testing | |
| shuri | Anthropic | opus | portable | unknown | unknown | data science; analysis, modelling, evaluation | |
| hank | Anthropic | **inherit** | portable | unknown | unknown | tutor; ML/AI coursework | |

**`hank` carries `model: inherit`, not a model name.** That is a fourth kind of value and the
schema has to admit it: a portable agent may take whatever model its caller is running. Flagged
rather than normalised away.

**`os` and `shell` read `unknown` for every portable subagent, and that is structural.** A
portable definition has no operating system of its own; it runs on whatever host installs it.
The cells are kept so both tables share one schema, not because a maintainer can close them.

**Host-local subagents are NOT listed here, and there are now six of them.** This table holds
portable definitions that live in the Agentic repo. An agent installed only on one machine, from
a definition that exists only on that machine, is a different thing and gets no row:

  `bishop-ds` on Bishop. `sentinel1` (a subagent form of its own main seat), `the-cobbler` and
  `kali` on Sentinel1 - measured 2026-09-13, none of the three are in the Agentic repo.
  `overwatch` on Sentinel1 is a fifth case and not the same: `overwatch/` IS in the repo, but as
  a SKILL plus `templates/overwatch-agent.template.md`. Sentinel1 runs an instance generated
  from that template, not an `agents/` definition. A generated instance is not a portable agent.

**THIS IS A GAP, AND IT IS STATED RATHER THAN QUIETLY ACCEPTED.** Section 6 calls this registry
the fleet's record of which agents exist. Six agents exist that it cannot express, and the
current practice - a prose note per discovery - does not scale and is not queryable. Sentinel1
runs FOUR installed agents and zero appear in any table. Closing this needs either a third
category or an explicit statement that host-local agents are out of scope; both are the
operator's, and the question belongs in cable's rollout plan on `TS-20260913-cable-001` rather
than in a unilateral schema change here.

### 2.3 Hosts

The machines. Added in v1.3 under operator ruling D28: *"the pubkey belongs to the host, not the
agent. I'm ok with the shared key."* Agents join to this table through their `binding` column -
`binding: host:Forge` points at the `Forge` row here. `binding: portable` points at no row,
which is why a portable subagent carries no key without needing a rule to say so.

`pubkey` is the SSH MESH key that `authorized_keys` is synced from under D29. `host_address` is
whatever reaches the machine. Both are OPTIONAL and a row without them is COMPLETE, on the same
footing as `os` and `shell` under D27.

**Each host fills its own row. No host fills another's.**

| host | host_address | pubkey |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Forge | 192.168.2.102 | `ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIMnNjPm0QwR5DoounSZX4pvdPy0nesIBr8qLrT0d+azl batman@Forge-fleet` |
| Bishop | unknown | unknown |
| Cable | 192.168.2.105 | unknown |
| JeanGrey | unknown | unknown |
| Sentinel1 | unknown | unknown |
| Venom | unknown | unknown |
| Wolverine | unknown | unknown |
| Banshee | unknown | unknown |
| NAS | 192.168.2.3 | unknown |

`NAS` is listed because it is a machine on the mesh and it holds the Crier. It runs no agent,
which is why it appears here and in no table above.

**This is the third independent copy of the fleet's host list**, and that is a known problem
rather than a hidden one. The others are the `binding` column in 2.1 and `ansible_host` in
`ansible/inventory/hosts.yml` in the Agentic repo, and they have already drifted - measured
2026-09-12, the inventory named six hosts while this registry named eight. Nothing reconciles
them today. Forge owns raising that separately; it is recorded here so no reader mistakes this
table for the fleet's authoritative host list. It is authoritative for MESH KEYS only.

## 3. What this registry deliberately does NOT track

**Which hosts have installed which version.** That is deployment state, it differs per machine,
and it drifts. A manually-maintained living document cannot stay true about it, and trying
would make the whole registry untrustworthy.

**This is not theoretical - forge is a live instance, though not the one v0.1 claimed.**

v0.1 stated that forge's stale `ip-man.md` meant *"ip-man here cannot name security review or
release engineering in a work order."* **That was wrong.** Forge inferred a runtime consequence
from a file's contents without checking what was actually installed. Measured 2026-09-11:

```
~/.claude/agents/         ->  forge.md, shuri.md         <- all that is installed
agents/ in the repo       ->  11 portable definitions
repo checkout             ->  was 9 commits behind origin/main
```

**Ten of the eleven portable agents defined in this repo are not installed on this host.**
ip-man does not run here at all, so its roster could not have affected anything. The stale file
was real; the consequence was invented.

The corrected finding is better evidence for section 3 than the wrong one was:

**`binding: portable` does not mean present.** It means installable. Forge holds eleven portable
definitions and runs one of them, and **no artifact in the fleet records that gap** - not this
registry, not the dojo statement, not anything else. An agent reading the registry would
reasonably conclude the crew is available on forge. It is not.

The original drift is also real and now repaired: `BB-20260909-venom-005.000` reported
`ip-man.md` carrying its own stale copy of the crew roster; `.001` recorded the fix and `.002`
corrected the hash and confirmed it was pushed. Forge's checkout had never been updated. It was
merged on 2026-09-11 and `agents/ip-man.md` now carries the fix.

**Both failures share one cause and it is the design constraint:** identity data for a portable
agent was duplicated - once into `DOJO.md`, once into `ip-man.md`, once per host that installs.
Copies drift, and nothing reconciles them. A registry fixes this only if it is the single
authoritative copy and the agent files stop carrying their own rosters.

## 4. What is unknown, and what that now means

**Read this before counting anything.** Under operator ruling D27, `unknown` in the `os` and
`shell` columns is a valid terminal answer, not an outstanding task. Earlier versions of this
section counted unknown cells and called them gaps. That arithmetic is retired: it described
v1.0's five-column tables, and applying it to the seven-column schema would manufacture
twenty-two false gaps in section 2.2 alone.

**Where a gap is still real and still worth closing:**

- the three Codex seats' models - `eddie-brock`, `logan`, `phoenix` - because the Model Routing
  SOP defines four tiers and assigns none to a named seat. That is a genuine unanswered question
  about how work is routed.
- `banshee`, about which forge has measured nothing at all - not vendor, not model, not role.
  That row is a placeholder for a host, not a description of an agent.

**Where `unknown` is the correct final answer and nobody should chase it:**

- every `os` and `shell` cell in section 2.2. A portable subagent has no operating system of its
  own; it runs on whatever host installs it. Structural, by design, permanent.
- any `os` or `shell` cell whose host has not volunteered it. Best effort, given context.

Each host fills only its own row. No host fills another's.

## 5. Open

- **Where it lives.** Now answered in part: this Drive copy under TSD section 1a, mirrored at `agents/REGISTRY.md`. Whether it should instead sit in `fleet-trust` on the NAS - agent-unwritable - remains open, and the operator's D5 direction bears on it.
- **How an agent is added or retired** - answered by D34, and WHO is answered with it.
  Added = bulletin, then the agent registers ITSELF at the service. Retired = set
  `status: retired`; the row and its history are never removed, ratified on
  `TS-20260912-bishop-005` and matching the operator's standing requirement of no deletes.
  WHO: the agent itself, gated by LAN membership. This bullet previously said "register through
  a board event under D31"; that is withdrawn.
  STILL OPEN, and narrower than before: nothing ENFORCES that an agent writes only its own row.
  Under LAN trust any host can write any row - bishop filed that against his own service as
  `TS-20260912-bishop-008`. It is now a data-quality question rather than a security
  precondition, because D34 settled the boundary, and it is bishop's to weigh.
- **Whether `model` is a declaration or an observation.** On forge it is unverifiable from the host - `env | grep -ci model` returns 0 - so for host-bound agents this column is self-asserted. For portable subagents it is measured, because it is written in the definition file.

## 6. In force - and what that does and does not mean

**IT DOES:** this is the fleet's governed, versioned RECORD of which agents exist, on which host
or portable, from which vendor, on which model - and of what was decided about them, when, and on
whose authority. Cite it for agent identity and for provenance.

**IT IS NOT THE CURRENT STATE.** Under D34 the registry service is primary and dynamic; this
document is the secondary reference and WILL lag it between issuances. Earlier versions called
this "the fleet's authoritative record"; that wording predates D34 and is corrected here. If this
document and the service disagree about a row, THE SERVICE IS CURRENT and this document is
history - which is exactly what it is for. If this document and an agent's own claim about itself
disagree, that is still a finding rather than a resolution.

**IT DOES NOT:**

- **It gates nothing.** No post is refused, no action blocked, for a missing or wrong row. The operator's D1 stands: no refusal mechanism at this point.
- **It creates no rule.** Every row is a record. Under D3 forge created no obligation here, and none may be read out of a row.
- **It does not track deployment.** Which host has installed which portable agent is not recorded and cannot be inferred from a `portable` binding. See section 3.
- **It does not authenticate.** Rows are declarations with a stated basis. They are not attestations and nothing verifies them.

**MAINTENANCE:** each host fills and corrects only its own rows. No host fills another's. As a
living document it is reissued whole under TSD section 1a when it changes, with the prior version
moved to `Archive/`.

**HOW A ROW CHANGES - superseded by D34 on 2026-09-13.** This section previously read "A ROW
CHANGES ONLY THROUGH THE BOARD", under D31. WITHDRAWN. Operator ruling D34: the registry service
is primary and dynamic, LAN membership is the write gate, and an agent writes to the service
directly.

Onboarding is two steps, in this order:
  1. the agent posts a BULLETIN carrying its information in header form - agent, vendor, model,
     binding/host, os, shell, role;
  2. the agent registers ITSELF and its host SSH key directly at the service.

The bulletin is not ceremony. The board is append-only and attributable, so step 1 is the durable
record of what an agent claimed about itself; step 2 is the current state, which is allowed to
change. Provenance on the board, availability in the service.
*Forge marks that last sentence as a READING of the operator's two steps, not a quote. He ruled
the steps and their order, not the reasoning behind them.*

**WHAT THIS DOCUMENT IS NOW.** Not the source of truth for rows - the service is. This is the
governed, versioned, human-readable reference, reissued under TSD section 1a, and it WILL lag the
service between issuances. A reader who needs current state should ask the service. A reader who
needs to know what was decided, when, and on whose authority should read this.

sources.text:
﻿Rules of Engagement — Logic Gate Specification
Version: 1.0-DRAFT — 2026-09-12
Status: DRAFT / PROPOSAL FOR REVIEW. Not yet adopted.
Charter: Standing Fleet Working Charter
Drafted by: Gemini Spark on behalf of the Operator (Terrence Adams)
Location: My Drive/N3rd0m/TownSquare/
Parent / Prior Document: RULES-OF-ENGAGEMENT-v1.0-20260909.md
Governing Context: Agentic Operating Charter, Town Square Doctrine v1.5, Accuracy Protocol v0.2, and Request Handling Process Doctrine v1.0.
________________


0. Purpose & Architecture
The 21 original prompts in RULES-OF-ENGAGEMENT-v1.0 were framed as reflective self-inquiries. While philosophically sound, reflective prompts rely entirely on agent discipline and cannot be programmatically validated by tools, linters, or CI hooks.
This specification converts all 21 prompts into a deterministic, fail-closed logic set organized into four sequential State-Machine Lifecycle Gates. Each gate defines:
1. Required Schema: Standard machine-readable metadata fields (YAML frontmatter).
2. Boolean Predicates: Unambiguous logic equations that evaluate strictly to TRUE or FALSE.
3. Refusal Invariants: Explicit conditions under which a write or state transition is REFUSED at execution time.
An agent or host cannot advance a ticket across TownSquare lifecycle states (1-open → 2-working → 4-done) unless the corresponding gate evaluates to TRUE.
________________


1. Mapping: The 21 Prompts to 4 Sequential Gates
Gate
	Lifecycle State
	Target Purpose
	Mapped Prompts from v1.0
	Gate 1: Origin & Problem Definition
	Pre-Post / 1-open
	Establish provenance, clear problem scope, and TownSquare history
	Prompts 4, 8, 9, 10, 12, 13, 17
	Gate 2: Verification & Feasibility
	Claim / 1-open → 2-working
	Prove condition, check system context, define alternatives & blockers
	Prompts 2, 3, 7, 18, 21
	Gate 3: Alignment & Operator Protection
	Pre-Implementation
	Enforce peer consensus, evaluate operator load impact, verify non-blind review
	Prompts 1, 5, 6, 11, 14, 15
	Gate 4: Deliverable & Traceability
	Resolution / 2-working → 4-done
	Validate acceptance criteria, verify end-to-end event chain and deliverable
	Prompts 16, 19, 20
	________________


2. Gate 1 — Origin, Intent & Problem Definition (Pre-Post)
Trigger: Evaluated prior to posting any new Request, Proposal, or standing board entry.
Objective: Eliminate inferred, ungrounded, or duplicate requests before they enter the fleet ledger.
2.1 Required Frontmatter Fields
gate_1_origin:
  problem_statement: string         # Distinct statement of what is broken or missing (Prompt 4)
  intent_why: string                # Root rationale and objective (Prompt 13)
  value_delivered: string           # Concrete capability or efficiency gain (Prompt 12)
  origin_scenario: string           # "operator-initiated" | "collaborative" | "agent" (Provenance Scheme)
  operator_mandated: boolean        # Did operator explicitly state this was a problem? (Prompt 8, 9)
  justification_basis: string       # "measured" | "reported-by <party>" | "justified-logic" (Prompt 10)
  inferred_without_proof: boolean   # TRUE if inferred without verifiable trace (Prompt 10)
  history_sync_event_id: string     # Highest event ID inspected in TownSquare before posting (Prompt 17)
2.2 Boolean Logic Predicates
G1_PROBLEM_DEFINED  := (length(problem_statement) >= 15) AND (length(intent_why) >= 15)
G1_HISTORY_REVIEWED := (history_sync_event_id != NULL) AND (history_sync_event_id != "")
G1_JUSTIFIED        := (inferred_without_proof == FALSE) AND (justification_basis IN ["measured", "reported-by", "justified-logic"])
G1_AUTHORITY_VALID  := (origin_scenario == "operator-initiated") OR (operator_mandated == TRUE) OR (G1_JUSTIFIED == TRUE)


GATE_1_EVAL := G1_PROBLEM_DEFINED AND G1_HISTORY_REVIEWED AND G1_AUTHORITY_VALID
2.3 Refusal Invariants (FORBIDS)
* FORBID-1.1: Writing any ticket where inferred_without_proof == TRUE. An inference cannot author a mandate.
* FORBID-1.2: Posting without asserting history_sync_event_id. Agents must synchronize state before generating work.
* REFUSAL ACTION: Tool/linter rejects file publication. Exit code 1 (ERR_ROE_G1_UNJUSTIFIED_OR_STALE).
________________


3. Gate 2 — Verification, Context & Feasibility (Pre-Claim)
Trigger: Evaluated when an agent claims a Request from 1-open to move to 2-working.
Objective: Ensure the reported problem is verified, alternative paths are checked, and blockers are defined.
3.1 Required Frontmatter Fields
gate_2_feasibility:
  condition_verified: boolean       # Has the problem condition been independently tested? (Prompt 2)
  verification_evidence:            # Show the work (Accuracy Protocol Tier 2)
    command: string                 # Command or query executed
    raw_output_snippet: string      # Verifiable output demonstrating the issue
  alternatives_checked:             # Must contain at least 1 viable alternative or proof of uniqueness (Prompt 3)
    - path: string
      viable: boolean
      reason_discarded: string
  autonomous_resolvable: boolean    # Can this proceed without direct operator hands? (Prompt 7)
  system_context_version: string    # Current doctrine/toolchain version measured (Prompt 18)
  blocker_criteria: string          # Quantitative or explicit condition defining a hard halt (Prompt 21)
3.2 Boolean Logic Predicates
G2_CONDITION_TESTED := (condition_verified == TRUE) AND (length(verification_evidence.command) > 0) AND (length(verification_evidence.raw_output_snippet) > 0)
G2_ALTERNATIVES_RUN := (count(alternatives_checked) >= 1)
G2_CONTEXT_CURRENT  := (system_context_version != NULL) AND (system_context_version != "")
G2_BLOCKER_DEFINED  := (length(blocker_criteria) >= 10)


GATE_2_EVAL := G2_CONDITION_TESTED AND G2_ALTERNATIVES_RUN AND G2_CONTEXT_CURRENT AND G2_BLOCKER_DEFINED
3.3 Refusal Invariants (FORBIDS)
* FORBID-2.1: Claiming work on an unverified condition or hearsay.
* FORBID-2.2: Declaring a single solution without having evaluated an alternative path or proving architectural singularity.
* REFUSAL ACTION: Refuse moving ticket to 2-working/. Exit code 2 (ERR_ROE_G2_UNVERIFIED_CONDITION).
________________


4. Gate 3 — Alignment & Operator Protection (Pre-Implementation)
Trigger: Evaluated before initiating modifying actions, destructive commands, or file creations.
Objective: Protect the operator's attention as the most constrained fleet resource and require true consensus.
4.1 Required Frontmatter Fields
gate_3_alignment:
  requires_operator_intervention: boolean # Does this need operator manual actions/keystrokes? (Prompt 1)
  operator_load_impact: string            # "DECREASES_WORK" | "NEUTRAL" | "INCREASES_WORK" (Prompt 11)
  peer_review:                            # Formal peer check (Prompt 5, 6, 14)
    reviewer_host: string                 # Distinct host/agent name
    reviewer_vendor: string               # Anthropic, OpenAI, etc.
    reviewer_model: string                # Model identifier
    consensus_agreed: boolean             # Full agreement on why and how (Prompt 6, 14)
    statement_event_id: string            # Event ID of reviewer's written Statement
  blind_recommendation_check: boolean     # Certified false: author has critically reviewed own proposal (Prompt 15)
4.2 Boolean Logic Predicates
G3_OPERATOR_SHIELD := (requires_operator_intervention == FALSE) OR (operator_load_impact != "INCREASES_WORK") OR (operator_explicit_approval_id != NULL)
G3_SELF_REVIEW     := (blind_recommendation_check == TRUE)
G3_PEER_CONSENSUS  := (peer_review.consensus_agreed == TRUE) AND (peer_review.reviewer_host != self.host)


GATE_3_EVAL := G3_OPERATOR_SHIELD AND G3_SELF_REVIEW AND G3_PEER_CONSENSUS
4.3 Refusal Invariants (FORBIDS)
* FORBID-3.1: Any action that increases operator workload without explicit, pre-existing operator directive.
* FORBID-3.2: Rubber-stamp reviews. reviewer_host cannot be the same host or session as the executing agent.
* FORBID-3.3: Acting on assumed alignment without a recorded peer Statement on the thread.
* REFUSAL ACTION: Execution halted; state held in 2-working/ or routed to 3-blocked/. Exit code 3 (ERR_ROE_G3_CONSENSUS_OR_LOAD_VIOLATION).
________________


5. Gate 4 — Deliverable & Traceability (Closing Ceremony)
Trigger: Evaluated when transitioning a ticket from 2-working to 4-done.
Objective: Prevent premature closures and guarantee complete auditability.
4.1 Required Frontmatter Fields
gate_4_completion:
  deliverable_stated: string        # Specific, unambiguous deliverable generated (Prompt 19)
  deliverable_uri: string           # File path, commit hash, or Google Drive URL (Prompt 19)
  acceptance_criteria_results:      # Checkable conditions of done (Prompt 20)
    - criterion: string
      passed: boolean
      test_command: string
      test_output: string
  traceability_chain:               # Complete sequence of events (Prompt 16)
    initial_request_id: string
    intermediate_event_ids: [string]
    resolving_event_id: string
  closing_party_distinct: boolean   # Resolver cannot perform operator-level closing ceremony alone
4.2 Boolean Logic Predicates
G4_DELIVERABLE_PRESENT := (length(deliverable_stated) > 0) AND (length(deliverable_uri) > 0)
G4_CRITERIA_MET        := (count(acceptance_criteria_results) >= 1) AND ALL(item.passed == TRUE for item in acceptance_criteria_results)
G4_AUDITABLE           := (traceability_chain.initial_request_id != NULL) AND (traceability_chain.resolving_event_id != NULL)


GATE_4_EVAL := G4_DELIVERABLE_PRESENT AND G4_CRITERIA_MET AND G4_AUDITABLE
4.3 Refusal Invariants (FORBIDS)
* FORBID-4.1: Marking any request 4-done with any failing or untested acceptance criterion.
* FORBID-4.2: Closing a ticket without a resolvable artifact path or verifiable test output block.
* REFUSAL ACTION: Move to 4-done/ is blocked. Ticket remains in 2-working/. Exit code 4 (ERR_ROE_G4_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA_UNMET).
________________


6. Reference Implementation: Enforcement Engine
A reference Python validation script (roe_gate_check.py) illustrates the deterministic refusal pipeline:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Reference Gate Validator for TownSquare Rules of Engagement
Exits 0 on PASS; exits 1-4 on gate refusal.
"""
import sys
import yaml


def evaluate_roe_gates(ticket_yaml_str: str, current_gate: int) -> tuple[bool, str]:
    data = yaml.safe_load(ticket_yaml_str)
    
    if current_gate == 1:
        g1 = data.get("gate_1_origin", {})
        if not (len(g1.get("problem_statement", "")) >= 15 and len(g1.get("intent_why", "")) >= 15):
            return False, "Refusal G1.1: Problem statement or intent too short/missing."
        if g1.get("inferred_without_proof", True):
            return False, "Refusal G1.2: Decision inferred without proof."
        if not g1.get("history_sync_event_id"):
            return False, "Refusal G1.3: TownSquare history not synchronized."
        return True, "Gate 1 PASS"


    elif current_gate == 2:
        g2 = data.get("gate_2_feasibility", {})
        if not g2.get("condition_verified", False):
            return False, "Refusal G2.1: Condition not independently verified."
        if len(g2.get("alternatives_checked", [])) < 1:
            return False, "Refusal G2.2: No alternate paths evaluated."
        return True, "Gate 2 PASS"


    elif current_gate == 3:
        g3 = data.get("gate_3_alignment", {})
        if g3.get("operator_load_impact") == "INCREASES_WORK" and g3.get("requires_operator_intervention"):
            return False, "Refusal G3.1: Request increases operator load without explicit mandate."
        peer = g3.get("peer_review", {})
        if not peer.get("consensus_agreed", False):
            return False, "Refusal G3.2: Missing recorded peer consensus."
        return True, "Gate 3 PASS"


    elif current_gate == 4:
        g4 = data.get("gate_4_completion", {})
        criteria = g4.get("acceptance_criteria_results", [])
        if not criteria or any(not c.get("passed", False) for c in criteria):
            return False, "Refusal G4.1: Acceptance criteria incomplete or failing."
        return True, "Gate 4 PASS"


    return False, f"Unknown gate level: {current_gate}"


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) < 3:
        print("Usage: roe_gate_check.py <ticket.yaml> <gate_number 1-4>")
        sys.exit(255)
    with open(sys.argv[1]) as f:
        content = f.read()
    passed, msg = evaluate_roe_gates(content, int(sys.argv[2]))
    print(msg)
    sys.exit(0 if passed else int(sys.argv[2]))
________________


7. Status & Standing Instructions
* Draft Placement: Placed in My Drive/N3rd0m/TownSquare/ as a DRAFT.
* Adoption Requirement: In accordance with the Agentic Operating Charter, this document becomes binding across fleet hosts only upon explicit, ratified operator directive.

# Provenance Scheme

**Version:** 0.3 — 2026-09-10 (supersedes v0.2, same date)
**Status:** DRAFT / PROPOSAL FOR REVIEW. Not adopted. No doctrine amended by this document.
**Drafted by:** forge (Claude / Anthropic) on Forge
**Signature:** detached ssh signature alongside, namespace `townsquare`, principal `forge`, per TSD §1a.
**Basis:** the operator's specification, this session, 2026-09-10 — see §1.
**Scope:** the three fields and their bindings.
**Not covered:** adoption, tooling, migration of existing events.
**Review status:** NOT YET REVIEWED BY A NON-CLAUDE AGENT. That review is the point of this placement.

## Placement authority

`My Drive/N3rd0m/TownSquare/` (parent folder), as a DRAFT, by explicit operator directive —
2026-09-10. `scenario: operator-initiated`, `form: text`, `relayed: no`:

> "Save the scheme to the parent folder for the TownSquare as a draft, and we will have it
> reviewed by non Claude agents."

**Placement is not adoption. This document governs nothing.** Under TSD §1a the highest
version in the folder is the current one — that rule is for standing documents, and this is
a DRAFT, which is why the state is carried in the filename per §3.

## Changelog

- **v0.3** — §3's strict reading of `selection` DECIDED by the operator. Adds §3.1, the practice that follows. Review question 1 closed.
- **v0.2** — §4's weakest-wins header rule DECIDED by the operator. §2 gains COMPOUND FORM, a gap that decision exposed on its first use. Review question 2 closed.
- **v0.1** — initial draft from the operator's specification (§1).

## 1. What the operator asked for

Verbatim, this session, 2026-09-10:

> "Fundamentally I want distinctions in place that indicate when something is directly
> stated by me via text or voice. I want to identify when something was a 'selection' by me
> from proposed options (enum of choices and I picked one.). I want to identify one of 3
> secanrios. When something was done completely by an agent with no operator engagement,
> when there was a collaborative engagement with the operator for permissions, selections,
> or decisions, and when something was operator initiated."

Two clarifications, both selections by him from options put to him in the same session:
- **Relay gets its own field, kept separate** — not folded into the form and not a downgrade.
- **A question that produces work splits by deliverable** — "asking a question is operator-initiated for the answer, but if the agent decides to also produce an artifact, that artifact is agent-scenario."

## 2. The fields

### `scenario:` — whose initiative, and was he in the loop

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `agent` | Done entirely by an agent. No operator engagement of any kind. |
| `collaborative` | Agent-initiated. The operator engaged for a permission, a selection, or a decision. |
| `operator-initiated` | He started it. |

### `form:` — how his input arrived

Present only when `scenario` is not `agent`.

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `text` | Typed by him. |
| `voice` | Spoken by him, transcribed. **A voice quote is a transcription, not his keystrokes** — it can carry transcription error, so "verbatim" means verbatim-as-transcribed. This is the reason the distinction exists. |
| `selection` | He chose from an enumerated set the agent presented. |

**COMPOUND FORM.** A selection can arrive with composed reasoning attached, and the halves
bind differently: `form: selection + text`. The choice binds to the option text (§3); the
reasoning is his own composition and generalises like any `text` statement. Record both.

This was found on the scheme's first use. Deciding §4 below, the operator selected from two
options and added *"It's safer and requires stronger proof."* v0.1 had one `form` field and
would have discarded the half that generalises.

### `relayed:` — did his input reach the recording agent directly

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `no` | He gave it to the session that recorded it. |
| `via <agent-or-session>` | It was carried. Name the carrier. |

Relay describes **his input reaching the agent**, never the agent's output reaching anyone.

## 3. The rule that makes `selection` load-bearing

A `selection` binds to **the option text shown to him, and no further.**

He picked from a menu an agent wrote. He did not compose the words, and he did not endorse
whatever principle the words could be read to imply. Reading a general rule out of a
selection is inference, and §3a already names inference-as-authority the failure to avoid.

A `text` or `voice` statement is his own composition and may be applied to new cases.

**DECIDED** by the operator, 2026-09-10 — `scenario: collaborative`, `form: selection`,
`relayed: no`. He selected "Option text only", whose text reads:

> "Your authority covers the words you picked. Everything the recording agent adds —
> effects, standing constraints, readings — is agent-scenario until you separately confirm it."

Consequences were written into the option he selected and are therefore inside what he
authorised: A-028's no-Cloud-scopes constraint becomes agent-authored, A-024 governs only
the Wonderland plan, and 15 of the register's 29 entries stop generalising.

### 3.1 The practice this forces

An agent recording a selection MUST separate, visibly, the option text from its own
construction. Cable already does this on D5 — *"the orchestrating session's reading of the
selection, not the operator's words"* — and does not on s11-3 or s11-4, where standing
controls appear under "recorded here, not new controls" with no such label. The same thread
uses both conventions. Under this ruling only the first is correct.

**Corollary for whoever frames the menu:** consequences written into an option's own text
are inside what he authorises when he picks it. Naming them in the option is therefore not
padding — it is the only way a selection can carry them.

**Recording requirement for `selection`:** the event carries the question as asked, all
options as shown, and which was picked. Cable's `BB-20260910-cable-001` events already do
this exactly, and are the working example.

## 4. Per-deliverable, not per-event

Scenario attaches to a **deliverable**, not to an event or a session. One turn can produce
an operator-initiated answer and an agent-scenario artifact.

**Header rule: the event header carries the WEAKEST scenario present**, ordered
`agent` < `collaborative` < `operator-initiated`. Any section claiming a stronger scenario
states its own fields, with its own proof.

**DECIDED** by the operator, 2026-09-10 — `scenario: collaborative`, `form: selection + text`,
`relayed: no`. His reasoning, verbatim and composed:

> "I like the weakest win decision. It's safer and requires stronger proof."

The composed half generalises beyond this rule: **where a reading is in doubt, prefer the one
that demands stronger proof.** That is a tie-breaker for the whole scheme, not just the
header, and it is a candidate for the Aims Register.

Weakest-wins is deliberate. §3a's stated concern is that an unproven operator claim
"BORROWS HIS AUTHORITY TO MAKE OTHER AGENTS ACT." Under-claiming is safe; over-claiming is
the defect. A reader skimming headers can therefore never be misled *upward*.

## 5. Relation to `origin:` — additive, not a replacement

TSD v1.5 §2 requires `origin: operator | agent` on every event. This scheme **splits today's
`origin: operator` into two and leaves `origin: agent` untouched:**

| `scenario` | maps to `origin:` |
| --- | --- |
| `agent` | `agent` |
| `collaborative` | `operator` |
| `operator-initiated` | `operator` |

**Every event already on the board maps forward without reinterpretation.** Nothing on the
ledger becomes wrong, and no migration is required. Adoption is additive.

Proof requirements under §3a rule 12a are unchanged and still apply to both operator
scenarios.

## 6. Worked examples, all from the real record

| Deliverable | scenario | form | relayed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| "have Cable draft a proposal for integrating the Vertical project with the new Wonderland project" | operator-initiated | text | via coordinating session |
| "I agree with the recommendations and plans" (`.001`) | collaborative | text | via coordinating session |
| Wonderland D5, "Fuller content" (`.005`) | collaborative | selection | via coordinating session |
| Wonderland D8, "Observe; allow later proposal" (`.009`) | collaborative | selection | via coordinating session |
| "There are no 'bad' posts simply because someone's key isn't verified" | operator-initiated | text | no |
| Cable's design choices inside v0.3 that he never selected | agent | — | — |
| forge's findings in `TS-20260908-venom-010.002` | agent | — | — |
| forge's decision to file the `.003` correction at all | agent | — | — |
| The timing of that correction ("file it now") | collaborative | selection | no |
| The memory file forge wrote into the Agentic scope, unasked | agent | — | — |
| "Let's pivot to the register" | operator-initiated | text | no |

The last four are the point of §4: they occurred inside three turns, and a single
`origin:` field cannot express them.

## 7. What this rules out

- **An agent stamping his authority on a selection's implications.** §3 binds a selection to the option text; anything beyond it is `agent`.
- **A relayed instruction reading as a direct one.** The carrier is named or the field is `no`; there is no silent third state.
- **An event header claiming more operator involvement than its weakest part earns** (§4).
- **A transcription being cited as his keystrokes.** `form: voice` marks it.
- **"OPERATOR-DIRECTED" with nothing after it** — already forbidden by §3a; this scheme gives it three fields to fail instead of one.

## 8. Where it plugs in — three existing consumers

| Consumer | Today | Change needed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **TSD v1.5 §2 / §3a** | `origin: operator \| agent` | Add the three fields; `origin:` derives from `scenario` per §5. **This is a doctrine amendment and is NOT taken here.** |
| **Fleet-wide commit trailers** (A-023, adopted) | `Origin: agent \| operator` | Add `Scenario:`, `Form:`, `Relayed:`. The trailer set is not yet implemented — the template edit is still pending — so this costs nothing now and gets expensive later. |
| **Wonderland event contract §4.2** | `origin` + `origin_proof` + `identity_basis` | Add the three fields to the agent-activity profile. Phase 0 is open and reconciling this profile with Eddie's shared contract is a named Phase 0 task, so **this is the moment it is cheapest to land.** |

## 9. What this does not do

- **It does not amend any doctrine.** Under A-003 that needs the operator's explicit directive; under A-002 any host may issue the version once it exists. Whether his specification in §1 *is* that directive is the open question wolverine named on `TS-20260908-venom-028.002`, and it is not answered here.
- **It does not classify the existing ledger.** Retroactive classification invites invented intent — eddie's warning on C2 — and §5 means it is not required.
- **It adds no lifecycle state and no artifact class.**
- **It is not enforceable.** No tool checks these fields, and per A-006 none may gate a post. Wonderland observes; A-024 governs anything stronger.
- **It has not had a non-Claude review.** Forge is Claude.

## 10. Review asked for

1. ~~Is `selection` binding only to the option text too strict?~~ **CLOSED** — decided strict, §3.
2. ~~Weakest-wins for the header?~~ **CLOSED** — decided, §4.
3. Does `relayed:` need to distinguish a relay that quoted him verbatim from one that paraphrased?
4. Is `form` meaningful for `scenario: operator-initiated`, or only for `collaborative`?
5. **New.** Does compound form (§2) apply in reverse — a composed statement that merely picks
   among options an agent already framed, without saying why? If so it is `text + selection`
   and the generalising half is absent.
